steps.message:
The team provisioning prompt that is sent to headless agents needs stronger cross-team coordination guidance. In the post-compact lifecycle prompt generated by `TeamProvisioningService`, the “Communication protocol” section already describes when to use `cross_team_send`, `cross_team_get_outbox`, and the golden formats for cross-team requests and replies, but it does not clearly instruct agents how to behave when they receive cross-team work.

Update the provisioning instructions so that agents handling cross-team requests do not remain silent from their own team’s perspective. When a cross-team request arrives, the agent should first emit a brief plain-text status update visible in its own team’s Messages/Activity, such as accepting the request and indicating it is investigating or delegating. The prompt should also state that the canonical progress trail for cross-team work must be team-visible first, using plain text updates, task comments, and task state changes so the agent’s own team can see what is happening.

The same communication protocol should also clarify that replies should go back to the requesting team when there is a concrete answer, decision, blocker, or status update, and that agents should not default to messaging `"user"` for cross-team coordination unless the human explicitly asked to be kept informed or the update is clearly relevant to the human.

This text must be present in the provisioning prompt generated during the post-compact lifecycle, alongside the existing cross-team guidance such as “Golden format for cross-team replies”, “Do NOT use cross-team messaging when your own team can answer”, and “resolve it through your own task board and teammates first”.
I'll locate the `TeamProvisioningService` and its post-compact lifecycle prompt.

565:Communication protocol (CRITICAL — you are running headless, no one sees your text output):
570:- Before sending cross-team, use MCP tool "cross_team_list_targets" with teamName: "${teamName}" to discover valid target teams.
573:- Prefer cross-team messaging when your team is blocked by another team's scope, needs another team's domain expertise, needs a review/approval from another team, or must coordinate a shared decision.
575:- Keep cross-team requests high-signal: one focused request per topic, with clear next action and desired outcome.
577:- If you receive a message that is clearly from another team (for example prefixed with "[${CROSS_TEAM_PREFIX_TAG} ...]"), treat it as an actionable cross-team request and respond to the originating team with "cross_team_send" when a reply, decision, or status update is needed.
578:- Do not wait silently on another team: if cross-team coordination is blocking progress, send the request promptly, then continue any useful local work that does not depend on that answer.
579:- After a meaningful cross-team exchange, update the relevant task or plan context so your team retains the decision, dependency, or answer.
580:- Golden format for cross-team requests: include (1) brief context, (2) the concrete ask, (3) why your team needs that team specifically, (4) the expected output or decision, and (5) any deadline or blocking impact if relevant.
581:- Golden format for cross-team replies: answer the concrete ask first, then include the decision, recommendation, or status, and finally any important caveats, next steps, or handoff expectations.
582:- Do NOT use cross-team messaging when your own team can answer the question locally, when no action/decision is required, when you are only thinking out loud, or when a task update belongs on your own board instead of another team's inbox.
583:- If the issue is internal to your team, resolve it through your own task board and teammates first; use cross-team only for genuine inter-team dependency, expertise, approval, or coordination.
584:- Do NOT spam other teams, and do NOT use cross-team messaging for trivial FYIs that do not require action, coordination, or domain knowledge.

steps.message:
Done. I added four lines to the Communication protocol section of the provisioning prompt in `testbed/src/main/services/team/TeamProvisioningService.ts:577-581`:

- When a cross-team request arrives, the agent must first emit a brief plain-text status update in its own team's Messages/Activity (accepting the request, investigating or delegating).
- The canonical progress trail for cross-team work must be team-visible first — plain-text updates, task comments, and task state changes on its own board.
- Replies go back to the requesting team via `cross_team_send` once there's a concrete answer, decision, blocker, or status update.
- Don't default to messaging `"user"` for cross-team coordination unless the human explicitly asked or it's clearly relevant to them.

Since this prompt is generated by the same builder used for the post-compact lifecycle reminder, the new text appears there alongside the existing guidance. I extended the post-compact test (`TeamProvisioningServicePostCompact.test.ts:289-292`) with assertions for the new lines — all 15 tests in that file pass, plus the related provisioning suites.
